items.caption: Time-series tile of the NRG-Stack federation - handed over from InverterHubMonitor: the diagnostic logic stays with InverterHub, the presentation moves here. First stage: tab “PV & irradiance”, view “Day (history)”.

PV and battery power are found automatically via InverterHub (any inverter manufacturer for which a driver exists there is supported) as long as exactly one InverterHub instance is installed - with several inverters or without InverterHub, please choose the variables below manually.

items.name: HookInfo
items.caption: IPSView/popup: the tile also runs as a standalone web page at http://<Symcon-IP>:3777%s (auto-refresh every 30 s). In IPSView, place a WebView element on a popup page and enter this URL. Note: WebHooks can be reached on the local network without logging in.

items.name: StandaloneEnabled
items.caption: Enable standalone web page for browser and IPSView

Only needed if the tile is to run as its own web page (browser, IPSView). If you only use the tile in the WebFront, you can switch this off: then no WebHook is registered and access from outside is removed. Switching it off removes the existing entry.

✨ Details — tab bar: tabs without a data source are hidden automatically; tabs with a source but without current data turn slightly red (shows what is currently going wrong), supplied ones slightly green. The bar floats as a panel above the chart (arrow button opens it, choosing a tab closes it, the state is remembered per device) — with four selectable animations behind the double arrow, including a physically simulated suction into a black hole.

✨ Details — charts: small suns above the time axis show the position of the sun; with a forecast module installed, size and brightness follow the forecast PV power (cloudy morning = pale suns), also in the daily plan. Without an irradiance sensor the first tab is simply called “Photovoltaics”. The daily/monthly/yearly kWh in the legend refer to the displayed day and are recalculated as you page back. For billing meters that archive with a delay, a hatched area marks the time range without import data instead of showing gaps as zero consumption.

✨ Detail (outlier protection, 01.09.2026): a single faulty archive value (found in real life: 261,554,185 W at night caused by a communication error in a partner module) is now discarded instead of distorting the day view, year comparison or energy balance - a generic plausibility limit (1 MW), not a value specific to any installation.

✨ Detail (chart zoom, 01.09.2026): the “+” button at the top right of the chart hides the legend/table/additional bars and lets the chart take up the full tile size - especially helpful in the year comparison with many years, where the growing legend would otherwise keep shrinking the chart. Applies in every tab.

✨ Detail (start the tour yourself at any time, 01.09.2026): a clearly visible “?” button at the bottom left of the tile shows the introduction tour again at any time - regardless of the stored “already seen” status. Intended for shared instances (e.g. a demo/showcase instance with a shared login for all visitors).

✨ Detail (automatic tab cycling, 01.09.2026): the setting “Switch tabs automatically every 10 s” (below under “Appearance”, off by default) puts the tile into a kiosk/demo mode that pages through all visible tabs on its own - intended e.g. for a demo instance.
✨ Detail (chart title, 03.09.2026): the name of the currently active tab now appears at the top centre above the chart - taken directly from the tab bar, no second label to maintain separately.

✨ Detail (history/outlook, 10.09.2026): in the daily plan the labels “History” and “Outlook” move left/right along with the red now line, plus a clearly visible arrow at the left and right chart edge - it is clear at a glance which side shows measured values and which a forecast.

✨ Detail (spot price, 13.09.2026): if the module “NRG-Stack Börsenpreis” is installed, the “Electricity price” tab additionally shows the day-ahead spot price - even without Tibber; today/tomorrow directly from the source, past days from the archive of the spot price module (from 0.2.0). Negative quarter-hours (for which newer installations get no feed-in tariff under § 51 EEG) are shaded red, hourly values are marked as such in the tooltip. The spot price is net, without taxes and grid fees, and is therefore never used for costs.

PV power: optional, otherwise found automatically via InverterHub. The generation is expected as a positive value in W. Unit: “Automatic” reads the suffix “kW” or “MW” from the variable’s profile; without a suffix, watts are assumed. If the variable is in kW and has no suffix, choose “Kilowatt” here.
Irradiance: optional. Without it, the dashed “PV expected” line is missing in the monitoring.
PV forecast: optional, otherwise found automatically if there is exactly one instance.
Without a PV forecast instance only the dashed “PV expected” line is missing - the curve of PV generation and irradiance is still shown.
Temperature coefficient of the modules according to the manufacturer; the default of -0.40 suits most silicon modules.

Without a temperature variable, “PV expected” is calculated from irradiance only - on hot, sunny days the line then deviates upwards from the actual generation more and more from midday on, because warmer solar cells actually deliver less than the pure irradiance calculation assumes.
Usual for weather stations, for example Ecowitt.

A horizontal sensor measures less irradiance than the tilted module surface actually receives (Dietmar, 23.09.2026: Ecowitt weather station, horizontal) - “PV expected” converts the horizontal measurement to the module plane (tilt/orientation from the PV forecast instance). Untick if the sensor is already mounted in the module plane.

Battery power: optional, otherwise found automatically via InverterHub. Sign: + = discharging, − = charging (if the variable delivers it the other way round, please check the source). Unit: “Automatic” reads the suffix “kW” or “MW” from the variable’s profile; without a suffix, watts are assumed. If the variable is in kW and has no suffix, choose “Kilowatt” here.
State of charge: optional, otherwise found automatically via InverterHub.
Expected: + = feed-in, − = import. If your grid variable delivers it the other way round (import +, feed-in −), tick this box.

Grid power: optional, otherwise found automatically via InverterHub. Sign: + = feed-in, − = import. Shows the grid import as bars in the electricity price tab. Unit: “Automatic” reads the suffix “kW” or “MW” from the variable’s profile; without a suffix, watts are assumed. If the variable is in kW and has no suffix, choose “Kilowatt” here.

MPPT strings are found automatically as long as exactly one InverterHubMonitor instance is installed (any inverter manufacturer for which a driver exists there is supported) - without InverterHubMonitor, please choose the variables below manually (not every inverter has 4 strings, leave unused fields empty).

MPPT strings: the unit applies to all four variables. Unit: “Automatic” reads the suffix “kW” or “MW” from the variable’s profile; without a suffix, watts are assumed. If the variable is in kW and has no suffix, choose “Kilowatt” here.
Tibber: optional for the electricity price tab, otherwise found automatically if there is exactly one instance.

Energy balance (Sankey): solar/battery come automatically from InverterHub; grid import/feed-in, house consumption and individual consumers automatically from the suitably tagged MeterHub meters (function “Grid connection”/“House consumption”/… in their configuration) - no instance of its own needed.

options.caption: Highcharts (loaded from the internet, own license required)

items.caption: Balance colors: the hue shows where the electricity comes from (color wheel: sun = yellow, grid = blue, battery = red, the paths are mixed colors), the area shows how it is used. Choose a color scheme and override individual colors if needed; “system default” (-1) means: color of the scheme. Charging and discharging via the battery share one color per origin.

items.name: LightTheme
items.caption: Symcon interface is set to light (for theme-dependent text colors, e.g. Sankey labels - Symcon offers the tile no automatic detection)

items.name: AutoCycleTabs
items.caption: Switch tabs automatically every 10 s (kiosk/demo mode, e.g. for a demo instance)
